text:
maria: quick check — running into a weird case where a route-level flag seems to override the org setting for a canary. org flag is false, route has it true and a 5% canary. Is that intended behavior?

aj: yes, by default the resolver picks the most specific scope (route > project > org). that said, there are supposed to be guardrails to prevent a route from enabling when the org explicitly locks a flag. do you have the config snippet?

maria: pasted the minimal example below, seen in prod config manager:```
org:
  enable_new_routing: false
  enable_new_routing_locked: true
route:
  enable_new_routing: true
  canary_pct: 5
```

maria: but routes are still serving the new path for the 5% cohort. :thinking_face:

aj: hmm. if enable_new_routing_locked is true the resolver should treat any narrower-scope TRUE as invalid unless overridden by an admin role. possible causes: 1) lock flag not propagated to the route namespace, 2) resolver bug where boolean locks ignored, 3) rollout created with "force" by the rollout service.

samir: fyi the rollout service will surface a `force` tag when an operator creates it via console. featurebot should have emitted a webhook. @featurebot any events? :eyes:

featurebot: rollout created r-2026-73 by maria — target: route/service-a — flag: enable_new_routing=true — canary: 5% — meta: created_via=console, forced=false

aj: OK console didn't force it. next step: check namespace propagation (org -> project -> route) in the flag-store. maria can you paste the route metadata (namespace attrs)?

maria: grabbing it now, but quick question — what's the desired policy here? if org locks a flag, should routes be blocked entirely or allowed to run a 0->5 canary with an explicit admin exemption?

ilana: from security/compliance: locks mean "deny unless admin-explicit-approval". we need an audit log and an approval flow. no silent route enablement.

aj: agreed. implementation plan I propose: 1) resolver checks .locked on ancestor scopes and returns DENY unless rollout has admin_approval=true; 2) console UI prevents creating a non-admin rollout when ancestor locked; 3) put a short-term alert that flags violating the rule trigger a warning in the console.

maria: sounds good. are we sure this won't break any existing rollouts where we intentionally let projects override org?

aj: we need a migration: treat existing route rollouts created before X date as grandfathered unless org explicitly flips the lock after the rollout. otherwise patch will be too disruptive.

samir: I'll own the migration decision and create a checklist. will include: list rollouts touching locked flags, owners, and suggested mitigation (rollback or admin-approve). ETA EOD tomorrow.

maria: thanks. I'll open a PR with resolver change + unit tests. pinging @aj for review and @ilana for the approval/audit bits in the UI.

aj: ping received — will review. if it's small I can merge and we can gate release behind a feature-ops toggle. :thumbsup:

ilana: I'll draft the audit message and the required fields for admin_approval (approver id, timestamp, reason). we should also add a KMS-protected signature for approvals later.

featurebot: alert: 1 rollout (r-2026-73) matches new locked-ancestry rule and is flagged for review.

maria: FYI I've paused the route canary in console until we confirm. thanks everyone.

aj: follow-up todo list: (1) maria PR for resolver + tests, (2) samir migration checklist, (3) ilana audit schema + UI change, (4) ops alerting for violations. I'll link issues in thread when created. :white_check_mark:

maria: linking issues now — will add reviewers. thanks!
